text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Committee proposes easing criminal law so all prison sentences less than two years would always be suspended, unless the crime is severe or the criminal has a record.
- Glorious weddings are in fashion and can cost tens of thousands of markka even if nothing special is included.
- Bankrupt insurer Kansa's U.S. subsidiary Clarendon is worth more than earlier believed, possibly returning "a significant portion" of Kansa's creditors' money.

- Parliament constitutional committee is debating whether changes in the Bank of Finland Act should be handled as a constitutional change, which would require two subsquent parliaments' approval or a 5/6 majority.
- Telephone bugging and other technical surveillance was legal until 1995, says security police chief Seppo Nevala.
- Tunnel between Stockmann department store and Forum shopping centre in central Helsinki opens.

- The future of state-owned Alko's alcohol retail monopoly may be determined by European Court ruling, after advisory opinion of Advocate-General Michael Elmer in a case against the Swedish monopoly said European law was an obstacle to it.

- The Coca-Cola company has changed its policy to replace local representatives with own distribution but has a dilemma in Finland which is small, scarcely populated and offers little economies of scale. Hartwall still in talks on distribution but has no comment.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Finvest's Interbank was rescued in 1994 through complicated financial operations by JP-Finance, the parent of the Poyry companies.
- A planned requirement for a 70 percent equity-to-assets ratio for real estate investment companies is too high, branch says.
- Consumer technology retailers and wholesalers expect growth to accelerate this year.
AAMULEHTI
- Sometimes lethal escherichia coli bacteria has found its way into Finland with seven infected last year.
- An environmental disaster in Paijanne Lake in central Finland four years ago now threatening to pollute Helsinki's drinking water.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Part of supreme court judges' activities to earn additional income are legally questionable, researcher shows.
- Top war criminals should not be taken into Finland's prisons, prison authority official says.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Shipyard subsidies are feasible in the short term, ministry of trade and industry study says.
- Insurer Pohjola's plans to take over mutual insurer Suomi may take longer than expected and the Suomi's surplus assets may have to be earmarked for its policy holders.
-- Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 242
